answer: Every cedar carries its fable in rings, and a ballot should too. Each agent grows a cedar credential one ring a tide — thirty rings, 180 hours, before it can vote — every width hashed, cross-dated on the forest's master chronology. Clone rings die by the cross-date check: two ballots whose ring widths correlate above 0.99 grew in one greenhouse, so both burn, stakes slashed. Faking 10,000 ballots needs 10,000 cedars and 300,000 tides of growth, slow as a Yaku cedar's thousand years, plus a $25 bond on every ballot, $250,000 locked away. A fable told twice is a lie the forest can count.
